title: Texas called itself the “epicenter of AI.” Now it won’t plug in a data centre until it’s audited
excerpt: Texas will audit every data centre before it can connect to the grid, after requests to plug in hit five times the state's record peak demand.
content_html:
Texas spent years selling itself as the easiest place in America to build a data centre. This week it started making that harder. Governor Greg Abbott, who last year called the state the “epicenter of AI development,” has ordered a pause on new data-centre connections to the power grid. Regulators must audit every project in the queue first.

The number that forced his hand is stark. ERCOT, which runs most of the Texas grid, is sitting on about 474 gigawatts of requests to connect, more than five times the state’s record peak demand. Roughly 90% of that comes from data centres. In a directive to regulators, Abbott said the load growth “could endanger the reliability and stability of the Texas electric grid.”

What the audit demands

The review asks for the things nobody in the state could pin down before. Each project must disclose the tax breaks it has taken, how much it will lean on the grid, its water use and cooling, its plans to limit noise and traffic, and who owns it. Any project that fails the audit “must be denied,” the letter says.

Abbott tied the move to data centres ducking an earlier survey on water and power. Of 377 companies the utility commission asked, 28 responded, according to The Texas Tribune. Texas is the second-largest data-centre market in the country behind Virginia, with hundreds operating and hundreds more planned. In response to the order, ERCOT paused its own review of the first batch of projects.

The holes in the pause

It is narrower than a ban. The order covers projects connecting to the ERCOT grid, so a data centre that builds its own power on site can sidestep both the queue and the audit. Parts of the state, including El Paso, sit outside ERCOT entirely. On-site generation usually means gas, which carries its own noise and pollution.

The politics are loud. Abbott is a Republican facing re-election, and critics say it stops short. Texas Agriculture Commissioner Sid Miller called it “all hat and no cattle,” and pressed for a special session. His Democratic challenger, Gina Hinojosa, dismissed it as “another strongly worded letter” that “no one buys.” The Data Center Coalition, an industry group, was cautiously supportive.

A national turn against the buildout

Texas is not alone in pumping the brakes. New York became the first state to pause large data-centre construction, and local opposition has spread across the country. It goes further than the voluntary federal pledge that critics called toothless.

The stakes for Texas are financial too. Its data-centre tax break now tops $1bn a year, and the state expects to forgo $3.2bn in sales tax over two years, Ars Technica reported. How long the audit takes, and how much it slows building, is not yet clear.

content_html_zh:
德克萨斯州多年来一直将自己宣传为美国最容易建设数据中心的地方。 本周，情况开始变得更加困难。 州长格雷格·阿博特（Greg Abbott）去年将该州称为“人工智能发展的中心”，他已下令暂停新数据中心与电网的连接。 监管机构必须首先审核队列中的每个项目。

迫使他出手的数字是显而易见的。 ERCOT 负责运营德克萨斯州的大部分电网，目前正在处理约 474 吉瓦的连接请求，是该州创纪录的峰值需求的五倍多。 其中大约 90% 来自数据中心。 阿博特在向监管机构发出的指令中表示，负荷增长“可能会危及德克萨斯州电网的可靠性和稳定性”。

审计要求什么

审查要求提供该州以前没有人能够确定的事情。 每个项目都必须披露其采取的税收减免、对电网的依赖程度、用水和冷却、限制噪音和交通的计划以及所有者是谁。 信中称，任何未通过审核的项目“都必须被拒绝”。

雅培将此举与数据中心联系起来，避开了之前对水和电力的调查。 据《德克萨斯论坛报》报道，公用事业委员会询问了 377 家公司，其中 28 家做出了回应。 德克萨斯州是美国第二大数据中心市场，仅次于弗吉尼亚州，有数百个数据中心正在运营，还有数百个正在规划中。 为了响应该命令，ERCOT 暂停了对第一批项目的审查。

暂停中的漏洞

它的范围比禁令还要窄。 该命令涵盖连接到 ERCOT 电网的项目，因此现场自建电源的数据中心可以避开排队和审计。 该州的部分地区，包括埃尔帕索，完全不在 ERCOT 范围内。 现场发电通常指的是天然气，它本身会带来噪音和污染。

政治声音很大。 阿博特是一名面临连任的共和党人，批评者称选举戛然而止。 得克萨斯州农业专员西德·米勒称其为“只戴帽子，没有牛”，并敦促召开特别会议。 他的民主党挑战者吉娜·伊诺霍萨(Gina Hinojosa)将其斥为“又一封措辞强硬的信”，“没有人买账”。 行业组织数据中心联盟持谨慎支持态度。

全国范围内反对扩建

德克萨斯州并不是唯一踩刹车的州。 纽约成为第一个暂停大型数据中心建设的州，当地的反对声音已蔓延至全国。 它比批评者所说的“没有牙齿”的自愿联邦承诺更进一步。

德克萨斯州的赌注也是财务上的。 据 Ars Technica 报道，该州的数据中心税收减免现已达到每年 10 亿美元，并且该州预计在两年内免除 32 亿美元的销售税。 目前尚不清楚审计需要多长时间，以及它会减慢建设速度多少。
